title: The Thiele Machine: No Free Insight
description:
I didn't invent a machine. I found one. That is my conviction. Take a blank cell and write a 0 in it, and keep it a 0: something is now the case that wasn't, and that moment, nothing becoming something, is never free. In any real device it gives off heat by happening, less the slower it goes but never none; keeping it is paid on top, in a merge, which carries Landauer's heat floor (a named premise) when the merged states were really possible, or in room never given back. The counting is proved on any machine, finite or endless; finiteness takes the room away and forces the merge. Certification, a record that a claim was checked and closed, is the sharpest case of a kept distinction.

The Thiele Machine is an abstract model of computation, a machine the way Turing's is: five parts (states, moves, a step, a price per move, a yes-or-no reading) and one rule, the toll: a step that turns the reading from no to yes costs at least one mark. It computes nothing a Turing machine can't. What it adds is a place, enforced by the step itself, for what a computation established and what establishing it cost. This work is an argument, made with that model, that an account of computation should carry that axis.

Proved, with every argument on the page and every premise named: anything that follows the toll pays to get from uncertified to certified (the universal floor). On a finite machine whose certificate is never taken back, the certifying step merges states, so the toll follows from pricing merges; a measurement that forgets nothing can be priced at zero marks, borrowing a blank page that is paid for when it is wiped. A window that shows a certifying step and a quiet one alike cannot price certification exactly. Over any base machine, an honest permanent record is a latch on an event; which event deserves it is the pointer thesis.

The witness is a minimal two-counter machine with CHECK, COMMIT and CERTIFY, where every raised certificate went through a passing check of exactly that claim. Thiele-complete asks for a universal base whose moves cannot touch the record, a record that stays up, blank starts, computing moves that cost no marks and every other move exactly one, and a run whose record ends up from one start and down from another, and nothing about what the record is about; every clock fails it, every universal base reaches it by adding marks, and every Thiele-complete machine hides its record and ledger from its own window. Certified Thiele-complete adds clean starts, a record raised only by an earned check, commitment and certificate of one claim, and a claim that can fail; the small machine meets it. A certified universal Thiele machine U, one fixed program of 3728 instructions of the small machine's own kinds, runs every program of the small machine from every clean start as a guest, every computing step a counter move of its host and every rise of its record placed by its program, with the guest's record earned again by U's own check, commit and certificate.

The repository contains the Coq development (the formal counterparts, a tool for catching mistakes), the small machine, the monograph (PDF and plain text), and the mathematical specification. An earlier virtual machine and hardware development is preserved at tag v3.3.0. The assumption receipt lists every statement and what it depends on: none depend on project-local or third-party axioms, only on named standard-library constants. Physical and foundational readings are stated as premises or conjectures, never as results.
